title: Search is not a door
takeaway: Never reach a mint site, wallet or app through search or ads. Use your checked bookmark or type the address yourself.

cards.title: The first result
cards.body: It is presale night and you cannot find the link. You search Pocket Dragons mint and the first result has the dragons, the right name and a countdown. In this practice, the real site is pocketdragons.example. Look at what the results really are before you tap.

badge.label: Paid ad
badge.why: Anyone can pay for the top spot, scammers included.

url.why: An extra word makes a different site.

cards.title: Drained this year
cards.body: This is not rare. In 2026 fake search ads emptied the wallets of people looking for some of the biggest names in crypto. Each one looked like the real thing and sat at the very top of the results.
points: Uniswap, February: a user lost a wallet worth mid six figures to a fake top result
March: SEAL blocked 356 scam ad links in 18 days, with over $1.27 million stolen
Uniswap, May: fake ads stole at least $400,000
Hyperliquid, August: one user lost about 550,000 USDC after a sponsored ad
Ledger, August: a fake ad led to a fake device check that stole recovery phrases

cards.title: The address on an ad can lie
cards.body: Researchers found a Ledger scam ad that showed google.com as its address. Others show the real brand name while a hidden frame loads the drainer. Scam pages also hide on trusted sites like sites.google.com, docs.google.com and free hosting, and they show safety checkers a harmless page. So a clean address on an ad proves nothing.
points: The address shown on an ad can be faked
A page on a big trusted site is not the brand's own site
Normal results can be fake too, not only ads

cards.title: The fake device check
cards.body: You search for your wallet app and the first result looks official. The page says your device is connected and asks you to confirm your 12 words. If you type them, it says invalid phrase and asks again. Both times, the words go straight to the thief.

sim.title: Device connected. Confirm your recovery phrase

cards.title: The safe path
cards.body: Search is fine for news. It is never the door to a mint site, a wallet or an app. Go in only through the door you checked yourself.
points: Use your bookmark, checked on two official channels
Or type the address yourself, letter by letter
Scroll past ads, or use an ad blocker
Get wallet apps and extensions only from the wallet's own site
Reached a site through search? Do not connect, sign or type your words

questions.stem: You search Pocket Dragons mint and the top result is a sponsored ad with the right name. What do you do?
options: Skip it and open your checked bookmark
Tap it, ads are checked by the search engine
Tap it but connect only your mint wallet
Tap it if the address looks right
questions.why: Fake ads have reached the top spot for Uniswap, Hyperliquid and Ledger searches in 2026. Search is never the door to a mint site.

questions.stem: An ad shows the address pocketdragons.example, exactly your bookmark. Is it safe to tap?
options: No, the address on an ad can be faked
Yes, the address matches
Yes, if it also says Official
Yes, if it is the first result
questions.why: Researchers found a Ledger scam ad that showed google.com as its address. Open your bookmark instead of the ad.

questions.why: A paid ad and a lookalike address are both red flags. Only your checked bookmark counts, and you do not need search to open it.

questions.stem: A page you found through search says your wallet is connected and asks you to confirm your 12 words. What is it?
options: A scam that steals your wallet
A normal security check
A step you need for the presale
A safe check because it shows your device
questions.why: A fake Ledger device check showed connection messages, then asked for the recovery phrase. No real wallet or site ever asks for your words.

questions.stem: You typed your words into a page and it said invalid phrase, try again. What does that mean?
options: Your words were stolen, move what is left to a new wallet now
Nothing was sent because it failed
You typed one word wrong, try again
The site is busy, try later
questions.why: The fake page sent the words to the thief and then showed an error so you would type them again. Treat the wallet as lost and follow I think I got drained.

questions.stem: A search result is a page on sites.google.com with the Pocket Dragons name and a Connect button. Is it the official site?
options: No, a page on a big site is not the brand's own site
Yes, Google hosts it so it is checked
Yes, if it has the logo
Yes, if it has many visitors
questions.why: Scam campaigns in 2026 used sites.google.com and docs.google.com pages to get past ad checks. Anyone can make one.

questions.stem: Which is the safest way to open the mint site on mint day?
options: Your bookmark, checked on two official channels
The first search result
The top sponsored ad
A link from a guide you found through search
questions.why: Security researchers advise saving trusted addresses as bookmarks and opening them directly, never through search.

questions.stem: You need to install a wallet extension. Where do you get it?
options: From a link on the wallet's own official site
From the first search ad
From a link in a guide on a hosted page
From a download link a helper sends
questions.why: Fake ads have pushed fake wallet apps and browser extensions. Start from the wallet's own site that you typed or bookmarked.

questions.stem: A scam ad gets reported and blocked. Is search safe again?
options: No, new ads go up again, sometimes within minutes
Yes, the search engine fixed it
Yes, for a week
Yes, if the ad is gone
questions.why: Researchers saw scammers relaunch with a new ad and landing page after a block, sometimes within minutes.

questions.stem: You searched by mistake and the page asks you to connect your wallet. What do you do?
options: Close it and open your checked bookmark
Connect only to look around
Connect your vault, it is safer
Connect and reject any popups
questions.why: Victims in 2026 connected and approved one transaction on sites they reached through ads, and lost everything. Do not connect, sign or type words on a site you reached through search.
